f: AI vs ML vs Deep Learning vs Generative AI
b: Nested circles: AI (machines mimicking human intelligence) ⊃ ML (learn patterns from data) ⊃ Deep Learning (multi-layer neural networks) ⊃ Generative AI (foundation models that create new content).
h: Russian dolls: the biggest doll is AI, the smallest one paints pictures (GenAI).

f: Supervised vs Unsupervised vs Reinforcement learning
b: Supervised: labeled data → classification/regression. Unsupervised: unlabeled → clustering (K-means), anomaly detection, dimensionality reduction. Reinforcement: agent + rewards via trial and error.
h: Supervisor gives answers; Unsupervised explores alone; Reinforcement = dog training with treats.

b: Classification predicts a category (spam/not spam). Regression predicts a number (price). Clustering groups unlabeled items (customer segments).
h: Class = Category, Regression = Real number, Cluster = Crowd groups.

b: Overfitting: great on training, poor on test (high variance, memorized). Fix: more data, regularization, early stopping, simpler model. Underfitting: poor on both (high bias). Fix: more complex model, more features, train longer.
h: Overfit = student memorized the answer key; Underfit = student never studied.

b: Bias = error from overly simple assumptions (underfitting). Variance = sensitivity to training-data noise (overfitting). Goal: balance (bias-variance trade-off).
h: Bias = darts all clustered but off-center; Variance = darts scattered everywhere.

b: Precision = TP/(TP+FP): of predicted positives, how many were right. Recall = TP/(TP+FN): of actual positives, how many were found. F1 = harmonic mean.
h: Precision punishes false Positives (spam filter). Recall Rescues every real case (cancer screening).

b: Accuracy = correct/total. Misleading on imbalanced data: predicting 'no fraud' always gives 99% accuracy. Use precision, recall, F1, AUC.
h: A broken clock saying 'no fraud' is 99% accurate.

b: Plots true-positive rate vs false-positive rate across all thresholds. AUC 1.0 = perfect, 0.5 = random guessing. Threshold-independent binary classifier metric.
h: ROC = Ranks Over every Cutoff.

b: MAE (mean absolute error), MSE (mean squared error), RMSE (root MSE, same units as the target), R² (variance explained, 0-1).
h: If the answer is a number, the metric has 'Error' or R² in it.

b: Set BEFORE training: learning rate, epochs, batch size, number of layers/trees, regularization. Tuned with SageMaker Automatic Model Tuning. Parameters (weights) are learned DURING training.
h: Hyper = knobs you turn; parameters = what the model learns.

b: Epoch = one full pass over the training data. Batch size = samples per update. Learning rate = step size of weight updates (too high diverges, too low is slow). More epochs can raise accuracy but risk overfitting.
h: Epoch = laps around the track; learning rate = stride length.

b: Business goal → ML problem framing → data collection/processing (feature engineering) → model development (train, tune, evaluate) → deployment → monitoring → retrain.
h: 'Big Frogs Don't Develop Dancing Moves' = Business, Frame, Data, Develop, Deploy, Monitor.

b: Training = learning patterns from data (expensive). Inference = using the trained model to make predictions on new data.
h: Training = studying; inference = taking the exam.

b: Real-time: low latency, persistent endpoint (≤6 MB, 60 s). Serverless: spiky traffic, no instances, cold starts. Asynchronous: large payloads ≤1 GB, ≤1 hour, queued. Batch transform: offline whole datasets.
h: Restaurant: Real-time = waiter; Serverless = food truck appears when needed; Async = catering order; Batch = meal-prep Sunday.

b: Studio (IDE), Canvas (no-code ML), Data Wrangler (visual data prep), Ground Truth (labeling), Feature Store (shared features), JumpStart (pre-trained models), Clarify (bias + explainability), Model Monitor (drift), Model Registry (versions/approval), Pipelines (MLOps CI/CD), Debugger (training issues), Model Cards (documentation), HyperPod (large-scale training).
h: Kitchen: Wrangler preps ingredients, Ground Truth labels jars, Feature Store is the pantry, Clarify is the food critic, Monitor is the smoke detector.

f: SageMaker Ground Truth vs Ground Truth Plus
b: Ground Truth: build labeling workflows with your workforce, Mechanical Turk or vendors, plus active learning. Ground Truth Plus: fully managed expert labeling workforce delivered by AWS.
h: Plus = AWS brings the people.

b: Applying DevOps to ML: version data, code and models; automate pipelines (SageMaker Pipelines); register models (Model Registry); monitor (Model Monitor); retrain on drift. Goals: repeatability, scalability, governance.
h: MLOps = an assembly line for models.

b: Data drift: input distribution changes. Concept drift: the relationship between inputs and target changes. Both degrade models; detect with SageMaker Model Monitor.
h: Data drift = new customers; concept drift = same customers, new habits.

b: CNN = images (convolution). RNN/LSTM = sequences (older NLP, time series). Transformer = self-attention, LLMs. GAN = generator vs discriminator. VAE = encode/decode via latent space. Diffusion = denoise noise into images.
h: CNN sees, RNN remembers, Transformer pays attention, GAN fights, Diffusion un-blurs.

b: NLP on text: sentiment, entities, key phrases, language detection, topic modeling, PII detection/redaction, custom classification and entities. Comprehend Medical = clinical text.
h: Comprehend = comprehends text.

b: Extracts printed and handwritten text, forms (key-value pairs), tables, and queries from scanned documents and PDFs. More than OCR.
h: Text-EXTRACT from paper.

b: Image and video: objects, scenes, faces, face comparison, celebrities, text in images, content moderation (unsafe content), PPE detection, Custom Labels.
h: Re-COG-nition = cognition for eyes.

f: Transcribe vs Polly vs Translate vs Lex
b: Transcribe: speech → text (diarization, custom vocab, Call Analytics, Medical). Polly: text → speech. Translate: language → language. Lex: chatbots (intents, slots, ASR + NLU).
h: Transcribe writes, Polly the parrot speaks, Translate converts, Lex chats.

b: ML-powered intelligent enterprise search across documents and connectors (SharePoint, S3, Salesforce). Can act as the retriever in RAG.
h: Kendra = knows where the answer is.

f: Personalize vs Forecast vs Fraud Detector
b: Personalize: recommendations. Forecast: time-series predictions (being folded into SageMaker Canvas). Fraud Detector: online fraud such as payments and fake accounts.
h: Personalize suggests, Forecast predicts the future, Fraud Detector catches crooks.

b: AWS Inferentia (Inf2): low-cost, high-performance inference. AWS Trainium (Trn1/Trn2): cost-efficient deep learning training.
h: INFerentia = INFerence; TRAINium = TRAINing.

b: Large model pre-trained on massive, broad, unlabeled data with self-supervision; adaptable to many tasks (text, chat, images, embeddings). LLMs are FMs for language.
h: A building's foundation: build many different houses on top.

b: The unit of text a model processes (word, sub-word or character; ~4 characters or ¾ of a word in English). Pricing and context limits are measured in tokens.
h: Tokens are like arcade tokens: you pay per token in and out.

b: Max number of tokens (prompt + response) the model can handle at once. Exceeding it fails or truncates. It differs per model.
h: The model's desk size: only so many pages fit.

b: Dense numeric vectors capturing semantic meaning; similar meaning → close vectors. Used for semantic search, RAG, recommendations, clustering. E.g. Titan Text Embeddings, Cohere Embed.
h: GPS coordinates for meaning.

b: OpenSearch Service/Serverless (vector engine, k-NN), Aurora PostgreSQL & RDS PostgreSQL (pgvector), Neptune Analytics, DocumentDB, MemoryDB, S3 Vectors; also Pinecone and Redis via Knowledge Bases.
h: Vectors live where 'k-NN' or 'pgvector' appears.

b: Temperature: randomness (low = deterministic, high = creative). Top P: sample from the top cumulative probability mass. Top K: sample from the K most likely tokens. Max tokens: output length cap. Stop sequences: halt strings.
h: Temperature = how wild the party; Top K = guest list count; Top P = guests until the room is P% full.

b: Plausible but false or unsupported output. Mitigate: RAG grounding, lower temperature, Guardrails contextual grounding checks, prompt 'say I don't know', human review.
h: Confident storyteller with no sources.

b: Advantages: adaptability, responsiveness, simplicity, creativity, productivity. Disadvantages: hallucinations, non-determinism, interpretability, bias, toxicity, IP/legal risk, cost.
h: Superpower with a fibbing habit.

b: Data selection → pre-training → optimization (fine-tuning, RLHF, prompt engineering) → evaluation → deployment → feedback and monitoring.
h: Pick ingredients → bake → decorate → taste → serve → reviews.

f: Pre-training vs Fine-tuning vs Continued pre-training
b: Pre-training: from scratch on huge unlabeled data. Continued pre-training: more UNLABELED domain data to add knowledge. Fine-tuning (supervised/instruction): LABELED prompt-completion pairs to teach task, format or style.
h: Unlabeled = learn knowledge; Labeled = learn behavior.

b: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback: humans rank responses → train a reward model → optimize the LLM with RL. Aligns models to be helpful, honest and harmless.
h: Like/dislike buttons training the model.

b: A large 'teacher' model's outputs train a smaller 'student' model, giving similar quality on a use case at lower cost and latency. Bedrock Model Distillation.
h: Teacher → student cheat sheet.

b: Fully managed, serverless API to FMs from Amazon (Nova, Titan), Anthropic, Meta, Mistral, Cohere, AI21, Stability, DeepSeek and others. Includes Knowledge Bases, Agents, Guardrails, Model Evaluation, fine-tuning, Prompt Management, Flows. Your data is not used to train base models.
h: Bedrock = bedrock foundation of gen-AI apps on AWS.

b: On-Demand: pay per token, no commitment. Batch: ~50% discount, async from S3. Provisioned Throughput: reserved model units (1 or 6-month or none), REQUIRED for custom/fine-tuned models.
h: Taxi (on-demand), bus (batch), leased car (provisioned).

b: JumpStart: deploy or fine-tune pre-trained and open models on SageMaker endpoints you manage (more control, in your VPC). Bedrock: serverless API, no infrastructure.
h: JumpStart = you drive the car; Bedrock = ride-share.

b: Free, no-code Amazon Bedrock playground to build and share gen-AI apps; great for learning and experimenting cheaply.
h: Party = play around, no cost.

b: Q Business: enterprise assistant grounded in company data (40+ connectors, respects permissions). Q Developer: coding assistant (IDE, CLI, security scans, code transformation). Q in QuickSight: natural-language BI. Q in Connect: contact-center agent assist.
h: Q = the gadget master in James Bond, one Q per department.

b: Micro (text, fastest/cheapest), Lite (multimodal, low cost), Pro (multimodal, capable), Premier (most capable), Canvas (image generation), Reel (video generation), Sonic (speech-to-speech).
h: Canvas paints, Reel films, Sonic talks.

b: Models handling multiple data types (text, image, audio, video). Multimodal embeddings put text and images in one vector space, enabling search with both.
h: Multi-sensory model.

b: Retrieve relevant chunks (embeddings + vector search) and add them to the prompt so the FM answers from current or private data. No retraining, fewer hallucinations, citations. On AWS: Bedrock Knowledge Bases.
h: Open-book exam: the model looks it up before answering.

b: Managed RAG: connect S3, web, Confluence, SharePoint, Salesforce → automatic chunking → embeddings → vector store → retrieval with citations. RetrieveAndGenerate API.
h: Plug in a library card.

b: Orchestrate multi-step tasks: the FM reasons (ReAct), calls APIs via action groups (Lambda + OpenAPI schema), queries knowledge bases, keeps session memory. Use to take ACTIONS (book, update, check status).
h: Agent = assistant with hands, not just a mouth.

b: Content filters (hate, insults, sexual, violence, misconduct, prompt attacks), denied topics, word filters, sensitive information (PII) filters, contextual grounding checks (hallucination), automated reasoning checks. Work across any FM.
h: Bowling bumpers for your chatbot.

b: Zero-shot (no examples), one/few-shot (examples), chain-of-thought (step by step), prompt templates, role/system prompts, negative prompts, prompt chaining, ReAct.
h: Show (few-shot), think aloud (CoT), role-play (system prompt).

b: Instruction + context + input data + output indicator (format). Be specific and concise, give examples, specify format/length/tone, use delimiters, put constraints in the system prompt.
h: ICIO: Instruction, Context, Input, Output.

b: Prompt injection (override instructions), jailbreaking (bypass safety), prompt leaking (expose the system prompt), poisoning. Mitigate: Guardrails prompt-attack filter, input validation, templates with guard instructions, least privilege for agents.
h: Social engineering for robots.

b: Prompt engineering < RAG < fine-tuning < continued pre-training < training from scratch. Always pick the cheapest approach that works.
h: Stairs: each step up costs more.

h: ROUGE = Reduce text (summary); BLEU = Bilingual.

h: Taste test before serving.

h: 'Fair Explanations Protect Safety; Control Verifies Good Trust'.

f: Model Cards vs AI Service Cards
b: SageMaker Model Cards: document YOUR models (intended use, risk, training data, evaluation). AWS AI Service Cards: AWS documents ITS AI services (use cases, limitations, responsible design).
h: Model Card = your model's passport; Service Card = AWS's product label.

b: Human review workflows for ML predictions, e.g. low-confidence Textract/Rekognition results or custom models. Human-in-the-loop.
h: A2I = AI + Eye (human eye).

b: Simple models (linear/logistic regression, decision trees) are transparent; complex models (deep nets, LLMs) perform better but are black boxes, so they need post-hoc explainability (SHAP, PDP).
h: Glass box vs black box.

b: Sampling bias (unrepresentative data), measurement bias, observer/confirmation bias, historical bias, algorithmic bias. Fix: diverse, balanced, inclusive, curated datasets; Clarify; human audits.
h: Garbage (biased) in → biased out.

h: Lawyers love gen-AI mistakes.

h: A dataset should look like the people it serves.

h: Trail = footprints; Config = before/after photos; Watch = heart monitor.

f: Artifact vs Audit Manager vs Trusted Advisor
b: Artifact: download AWS and ISV compliance reports (SOC, ISO, PCI), with email notifications. Audit Manager: continuously collect YOUR evidence against frameworks. Trusted Advisor: best-practice checks (cost, security, idle resources like underused Comprehend endpoints).
h: Artifact = AWS's report card; Audit Manager = your report card; Trusted Advisor = coach.

b: VPC interface endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) let VPCs reach Bedrock/SageMaker without internet. Gateway endpoints for S3/DynamoDB. SageMaker network isolation blocks training containers from the internet.
h: PrivateLink = private tunnel, no internet.

b: Data lifecycle, retention (S3 Lifecycle), residency (Region choice), lineage (origin and transformations), cataloging (Glue Data Catalog, DataZone), access control (Lake Formation), logging and monitoring.
h: Know where data came from, who touches it, where it lives, when it dies.

h: 42001: '42' is the answer to AI governance.
